title: The Wild Orchid on the Cliffside (U Tiewdohmaw Ha Shiteng Riat)
cultural_context: Poetic masterpiece using the rare cliff-clinging orchid (Tiewdohmaw) as an emblem of enduring modest virtue, from 'Ki Jingrwai Khasi'.
lyrics_khasi:
Ha shiteng riat ba piah
U tiewdohmaw u phuh,
Khlem thapbalang ban thiah,
Khlem briew ban leit kynruh;
U sngewbha tang ban paw
Ha kliar u mawsiang;
U kynud sur jingshai
Ha lyer ba pyngngad.

Wat la lyndet u lyoh
U shong ha ka jingjar,
Ka suid-tiew jong u don
Ka jingiwbih ba thiang;
Ki blei lum ki sngewbha
Ban iohi ia u;
Kum u tiew dohmaw shisha
Man ka dohnud bakhuid.
lyrics_english:
Midway down the sheer cliff
The wild rock-orchid blooms,
Without butterflies to rest on it,
Without human hands to touch it;
Content merely to shine
Upon the rocky ledge;
Humming a melody of light
In the pure refreshing breeze.

Though behind veil of clouds
It dwells in sacred quietude,
The gentle nectar of its blossom
Carries the sweetest fragrance;
The deities of the peaks rejoice
To gaze upon its grace;
Like the true cliff orchid
Is every pure, virtuous heart.

english: Without butterflies to rest on it,
Without human hands to touch it;
The gentle nectar of its blossom
The deities of the peaks rejoice
